newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Iraqi boats open fire at Kuwaiti patrols - agency.
newsitem.headline: Iraqi boats open fire at Kuwaiti patrols - agency.

text.p: Kuwait's Interior Ministry said three Iraqi vessels fired on its coast guard patrol boats in a demilitarised zone between the two countries, the official Kuwait News Agency reported late on Sunday.

"Two of the department's patrols and another belonging to the communications ministry were subjected to direct fire from three Iraqi boats at Khor Boubyan in the demilitarised zone," it said, quoting a ministry statement.
No injuries were reported in the incident, said the agency, which did not say when it happened.
The agency said the United Nations Iraq-Kuwait Observation Mission had been informed. UNIKOM monitors a demilitarised strip straddling the border of the two countries since the 1991 Gulf War.
Iraq invaded Kuwait in August 1990 and held it for seven months before a U.S.-led coalition drove out Baghdad's troops.
